title: Keep filters and paging in the URL

contentBlocks.body:
**Objective.** Make a filtered inventory view reloadable and shareable within the local app.

This is a real project lab in projects/inventory-desk, also available from the Projects page as a source download. Work in an isolated copy of the reference project so you can compare your change with a known baseline. Read ui/main.jsx; InventoryDesk.Api/Program.cs before editing. Trace one request from the UI or test through the boundary that owns the behavior.

contentBlocks.code:
dotnet test InventoryDesk.Tests --filter Milestone=07
npm run test:e2e

contentBlocks.body:
**Acceptance criteria.** Filtering updates the total count, page two contains the correct ordered row, ties use id as a stable secondary key, and the UI URL preserves search/sort/page.

**Make a meaningful variation.** Add a browser test that reloads a filtered URL and sees the same results. Add a secondary sort test with equal prices. Write the observable expectation before editing the implementation. If the variation exposes a defect, keep the smallest failing fixture as a regression test.
Review rubric: Server inputs are bounded, ordering is deterministic, and changing a filter resets an out-of-range page.

**Explain the boundary.** Why must sorting include a tie-breaker? Describe both a successful case and a rejected or missing-data case. Compare actual output with the acceptance criteria, including status codes, persisted values, and user-visible feedback where relevant.

**Evidence to keep.** Save the focused test result, a short before/after diff, and a note explaining one tradeoff. Completing the quiz records this lesson's concepts; it does not run the companion checks or certify that the project milestone is finished.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Why must sorting include a tie-breaker?

choices: Equal primary sort values still need a stable order
To hide matching rows from later pages
payload.answer: Equal primary sort values still need a stable order
